title: Why the distinctions of grace must be set out
source_text: THESIS I. AD intelligentiam & elucidationem multarum quaestionum, quae circa gratiam & liberum arbitrium, magna contentione animorum, agitantur, plurimum conducit nosse varias acceptiones & distinctiones gratiae, quae usitatae sunt in Scholis Christianis. Itaque non parum facit ad scopum nostrum, qui est lucem aliquam inferre controversiis illis, quae Scholas Christianas exercent & dividunt, si acceptiones & distinctiones istas, quantum fieri poterit, breviter & dilucide exponamus.
pass_a_gloss: THESIS I. For the understanding and elucidation of many questions, which concerning grace and free choice, with great contention of minds, are agitated, it conduces very much to know the various acceptations and distinctions of grace, which are in use in the Christian Schools. And so it does not do little for our aim, which is to bring some light to those controversies, which exercise and divide the Christian Schools, if we set out those acceptations and distinctions, as far as can be done, briefly and clearly.
pass_b_english: Thesis I. Many questions about grace and free choice are argued with great heat, and to understand and clear them up it helps a great deal to know the various senses and distinctions of grace used in the Christian schools.
Our aim is to throw some light on the controversies that occupy and divide those schools. So it will serve that aim well if we set out these senses and distinctions as briefly and clearly as we can.
